title: Quarterly cadence and contingency heatmap for hosted endpoint lineup and model rotations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: define a concrete quarterly cadence for hosted endpoint lineup changes (adds/rotations/deprecations), produce an operations-ready contingency heatmap for traffic and capacity failures, and create the scheduling guidance for canaries and rollbacks.

Background: The hosted model catalog and endpoint tiers have grown faster than our scheduling/playbook maturity. We need a lightweight, repeatable cadence that balances business commitments, SLA expectations, and engineering bandwidth while minimizing regressions after model swaps. This ticket consolidates PM decisions, runbook inputs from Reliability, and rollout thresholds for Dedicated/Hosted customers.

Scope:
- Ownership: PM owns cadence design; Eng owns rollout mechanics and gating; DX/Design owns user-facing communication templates.
- Outputs: cadence calendar, cadence-to-release mapping (what kinds of model changes go in which lane), contingency heatmap mapped to capacity tiers, a minimal config template for console rollout policies, and a set of acceptance/rollback criteria.
- Out of scope: deep rework of model evaluation pipeline (separate initiative).

Why now: Several upcoming model additions (~8 new variants across LlamaX and Redwood-neo) and a Dedicated capacity contract renewal require clearer scheduling and risk controls to reduce incident surface and customer surprise.
success_metrics: Reduce post-rollout customer-impacting regressions by 50% vs previous quarter
All hosted model swaps execute within agreed SLA windows 95% of the time
Canary rollback executes within target 15m mean time in 90% of trials
Runbook accepted by Eng + IR teams and published to ops wiki
deliverables: Quarterly cadence calendar (weeks -> lanes) in shared calendar
Contingency heatmap PDF mapping traffic tier vs. fallback strategy
Console rollout policy templates (canary %, duration, auto-fallback rules)
Acceptance/rollback checklist and example playbook for a LlamaX model swap
Postmortem template and tagging guidelines for model-swap incidents
